questions.q: What does 'deferred' revenue recognition mean for a transaction line?
options: Revenue is spread across multiple accounting periods using a revenue scheduling rule, instead of recognized all at once
The invoice is not sent until the revenue is earned
The customer does not have to pay until revenue is recognized
The transaction cannot be completed until the contract ends
questions.explain: Deferred recognition spreads revenue over time to match when the obligation is actually delivered, independent of invoice or payment timing.

questions.q: Does deferring revenue recognition change when an invoice is sent or when cash is collected?
options: Yes, deferred revenue means the invoice is delayed until revenue is earned
No — invoicing and payment timing follow the transaction and payment terms; recognition timing is a separate accounting decision
Yes, deferred revenue means the customer cannot be invoiced at all
No, but it does change the customer's credit limit
questions.explain: A contract can be invoiced in full upfront while its revenue is recognized gradually — billing and recognition are independent.

questions.q: What is a 'daily revenue rate' scheduling rule used for?
options: Charging daily late fees
Calculating daily interest on overdue balances
Recognizing revenue based on the actual number of days in each period, handling partial first/last periods more precisely than a fixed split
Setting the customer's payment term due date
questions.explain: The daily revenue rate method prorates recognition by actual days, which is more precise than a flat equal-period fixed schedule.

questions.q: Where does the unrecognized portion of deferred revenue sit until it's earned?
options: In a Revenue account
In the customer's credit limit
It is not recorded anywhere until fully earned
In an Unearned Revenue account (a liability)
questions.explain: Unearned revenue is a liability representing an obligation still owed to the customer; it moves to revenue as each period is recognized.

questions.q: In the Harborline Retail Group maintenance contract example, what happened at the invoice's completion in January?
options: The full $12,000 was booked as a debit to Accounts Receivable and a credit to Unearned Revenue
$12,000 of revenue was recognized immediately
No accounting entry was created until the contract ended
$1,000 was recognized and the remaining $11,000 was written off
questions.explain: The full invoice amount books to Unearned Revenue at completion; revenue is only recognized incrementally as each month's recognition process runs.
